title: Phaser
summary: Notes for using Game Arts files in Phaser 3. Written from the current documentation pages and the animation and easing source files read on 2026-10-24; nothing was run in a browser, so every mapping is documented, none is observed.

documented_against.engine_version: 3.60 or later (the pages read are the current unversioned documentation)

import_guidance.text: Export with `scripts/export_exchange.py --atlas <sheet>.atlas.json --format aseprite-array --frame-names index`, load it with the Aseprite loader and call createFromAseprite: every tag becomes an animation of the same name. Tags do not carry a loop, so say whether each loops when you play it.
Set the game config's pixelArt option to true: it turns antialiasing off and rounds drawn positions to whole pixels.
Leave antialias on (its default) so scaled and rotated textures are drawn with linear interpolation.
Use the runtime copies the framework derives (real transparency instead of the magenta background) as your textures, and the matching atlas data for frame rectangles and pivots.
The framework's ease_in, ease_out and ease_in_out are Phaser's Quadratic In, Out and InOut. The framework's cubic curve has no Phaser counterpart.

concept_map.engine_term: an atlas frame's frame {x, y, w, h}, in the JSON that load.atlas or load.aseprite reads
concept_map.note: Phaser reads TexturePacker-style frame data (frame, trimmed, sourceSize, spriteSourceSize, rotated, pivot). The framework's aseprite-array and aseprite-hash exports write those fields.

concept_map.engine_term: an atlas frame's custom pivot {x, y}, a custom origin
concept_map.note: The page documents an optional custom pivot per frame. The framework's exchange export writes the pivot as a fraction of the source picture.

concept_map.engine_term: the frame's duration in milliseconds, summed into the animation's duration
concept_map.note: createFromAseprite reads each frame's duration. A frame without one falls back to the largest safe integer, so every frame must carry its duration, which the export does.

concept_map.engine_term: AnimationManager.createFromAseprite: one animation per frame tag, named by the tag
concept_map.note: Since 3.50.0. The export needs the tags in meta and the item filename to be only the frame number: the source finds each frame by its number as text, so export with --frame-names index.

concept_map.engine_term: a frame tag with direction reverse: the frames are reversed
concept_map.note: Read from createFromAseprite's source.

concept_map.engine_term: a frame tag with direction pingpong: the animation's yoyo is set
concept_map.note: pingpong_reverse is not handled and plays forward without yoyo, so a pingpong_reverse tag needs your own handling.

concept_map.engine_term: not read from a tag: the game sets repeat when it plays the animation
concept_map.note: The created animation holds only its key, frames, duration and yoyo, so whether a tag loops is the game's decision.

concept_map.engine_term: not read from a tag
concept_map.note: A tag's repeat is ignored by createFromAseprite; the game counts plays.

concept_map.engine_term: game config pixelArt: true (antialias false and roundPixels true)
concept_map.note: The page calls it the best setting for pixel-art games.

concept_map.engine_term: game config antialias: true (the default), linear interpolation in WebGL
concept_map.note: The default.

concept_map.engine_term: game config width and height in game pixels, and the scale configuration
concept_map.note: The page gives 1024 by 768 as the defaults.

concept_map.engine_term: the NineSlice game object: leftWidth, rightWidth, topHeight, bottomHeight
concept_map.note: Since 3.60.0. The order differs from the framework's [left, top, right, bottom]: map the second and third values. A top and bottom of zero make a three-slice object.

concept_map.engine_term: Phaser.Math.Easing.Quadratic In, Out and InOut
concept_map.note: Read from the three source files: In is v * v, Out is v * (2 - v), and InOut is 0.5 * v * v after doubling below one and the mirrored form above. They equal the framework's ease_in, ease_out and ease_in_out.

concept_map.engine_term: Phaser.BlendModes.NORMAL
concept_map.note: The default.

concept_map.engine_term: Phaser.BlendModes.ADD
concept_map.note: In both the canvas and WebGL renderers.

concept_map.engine_term: Phaser.BlendModes.MULTIPLY
concept_map.note: In both the canvas and WebGL renderers.

concept_map.engine_term: Phaser.BlendModes.SCREEN
concept_map.note: In both the canvas and WebGL renderers.

concept_map.engine_term: no subtract blend mode is listed
concept_map.note: DIFFERENCE is a different operation; a shader or a different treatment is needed.

concept_map.engine_term: no premultiplied-alpha blend mode is listed
concept_map.note: The page says nothing about premultiplied alpha.

concept_map.engine_term: a game object's scrollFactor
concept_map.note: 1 moves with the camera, 0 does not move, and values between give partial movement. Scroll factors other than 1 are ignored by physics collisions.
